source.title: Primary School Curriculum Design — Creative Arts, Grade 6 (First Published 2017, Revised 2024)
source.notes: Read directly from grade-6-curriculum-desings/GRADE-6-CREATIVE-ARTS-Curriculum-Designs.pdf via the Read tool (no pages param), full text, all 3 strands + optional sub-strand + assessment rubrics + Appendix II resources table. Official Grade 6 subject name is 'Creative Arts' (not 'Creative Arts & Sports' — that title only applies to Grades 7-9), per namesByGrade in curriculum.ts. Essence statement: Creative Arts at this level integrates Art and Craft, Music, and Physical Health Education as one learning area.

subStrands.name: 1.1 String Musical Instruments and Drawing
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify string instruments from different indigenous communities in Kenya
Describe the functions of the parts of a string instrument
Make a fiddle using recyclable materials
Identify pictures drawn using stippling technique
Draw a picture of a musical instrument using stippling technique
Value indigenous string instruments drawn from indigenous communities in Kenya
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are indigenous string musical instruments necessary in music?
How is overlapping achieved in still-life drawing?
learningExperiences: Observe videos/pictures or real indigenous Kenyan string instruments and name the instrument, identify the community of origin and method of playing
Name parts of a string instrument from different indigenous communities in Kenya and explain their function(s)
Visit an institution or a cultural resource centre in the community/virtual site to familiarise themselves with Kenyan indigenous string instruments
Assemble tools and material from the locality and make a fiddle while observing safety
Brainstorm on ways of care for and maintenance of a string instrument and discuss the importance of doing so
Research and identify a drawing done using stippling technique
Draw a still-life composition of any two string musical instruments using stippling technique with emphasis on: overlapping, balance of forms, tone/texture
Value others' ideas as they talk about their own and others' displayed work
coreCompetencies: Creativity and imagination — comes up with new ideas of arranging forms to create a composition in still-life drawing and make a fiddle
Communication and Collaboration — values others' ideas as they talk clearly about displayed work
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — identifies string instruments from different Kenyan communities
Indigenous Languages — names string instruments using indigenous names as used in their communities of origin
scopeNotes: include: name, community of origin, method of playing, parts and functions, and care (handling/cleaning/storage) of string instruments
include: drawing technique is specifically stippling (dot-density texture/tone), applied to overlapping still-life composition, balance of forms
subStrands.notes: Split into 2 skills in this build: string-instrument identification/care/making (music/craft side) and stippling drawing technique (visual art side) — two genuinely distinct techniques named in one sub-strand.

subStrands.name: 1.2 Painting and Collage
specificLearningOutcomes: Classify colour categories on the colour wheel for familiarity
Paint a still life composition using brush stroke technique
Mount the painting using mat technique for display
Create a collage composition to apply the characteristics
Appreciate painting and collage techniques
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is mounting of pictures important?
learningExperiences: Mix and paint a colour wheel to represent primary, secondary and tertiary colours
Mix and paint a surface to create tonal gradation by thinning same tone/adding dark tone
Illustrate painting to create varied texture focusing on brush position/angle, brush load and brush strokes
Paint any two objects overlapping inspired by football game (tone and texture)
Source for mounting materials and tools (papers, glue, cutting tools)
Prepare the picture and mat surface by measuring and cutting
Attach the picture on the mat surface (centred position)
Explore actual/virtual samples of collage pictures to discuss characteristics: multi/mixed media and texture
Collect and prepare materials for making collage with focus on texture and type of the materials, adhesives, and support
Collaboratively make a collage with a theme 'football' to apply the characteristics
Talk about own and others' work
coreCompetencies: Critical thinking and problem solving — explores multiple perspectives of painting using varied tools and materials for creativity
Creativity and imagination — applies creative skills in selecting media for painting, and painting the still life composition
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — prepares the picture and mat surface by measuring and cutting
scopeNotes: include: colour wheel classification is specifically primary/secondary/tertiary categories
include: painting inspiration is explicitly a football-game theme (two overlapping objects); collage theme is also explicitly 'football'
subStrands.notes: Split into 2 skills: painting technique (colour wheel, brush stroke, tonal gradation, mounting) and collage (multi/mixed media, texture, football theme) — two named distinct techniques.

subStrands.name: 1.3 Volleyball
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify the serving and the digging skills in Volleyball
Perform under-arm service for skill acquisition
Execute single hand dig pass in volleyball for skill acquisition
Appreciate playing Volleyball game for enjoyment
keyInquiryQuestions: How can service skills in Volleyball be used to win a game?
learningExperiences: Watch a real or virtual Volleyball game responsibly to identify serving and digging skills
Demonstrate the under-arm service
Practise the under-arm in volleyball game
Demonstrate the single hand dig pass in volleyball
Practise the single hand dig pass in a game situation
Play a Volleyball game while applying the skills learnt and observing safety
Share own and others performance in Volleyball game while giving each other feedback
coreCompetencies: Learning to learn — acquires new skills of serving and the single hand dig pass in Volleyball game
Digital literacy — uses digital technology to source virtual Volleyball game to identify skills
linkedLearningAreas: Integrated Science — applies force while serving the Volleyball
scopeNotes: include: exactly two named skills — under-arm service, and single-hand dig pass (not double-hand/forearm dig)
subStrands.notes: Kept as one skill — a single cohesive game with two named skills, not two distinct techniques worth splitting.

subStrands.name: 1.4 Rhythm and Pattern Making
specificLearningOutcomes: Interpret rhythmic patterns in music
Compose a rhythm using a combination of musical notes and their rests
Improvise a rhythm in three-beat pattern on a percussion instrument
Prepare a block with a geometrical motif for printing a pattern
Print a full repeat pattern using a block for rhythm acquisition
Value rhythmic patterns created by self and others
keyInquiryQuestions: Why create rhythm in different beat patterns?
learningExperiences: Listen to/sing familiar songs and identify words with the French rhythm names taa, ta-te, taa-aa, taa-aa-aa, taa-aa-aa-aa
Tap/clap/stamp and recite rhythmic patterns using French rhythm names
Relate the French rhythm names to the music note symbols for the crotchet, pair of quavers, minim, dotted minim, semibreve and their rests
Apply composition techniques to compose original rhythmic patterns using French rhythm names or note symbols, and their rests
Use digital resources to further their skills of creating rhythms
Listen to songs and identify songs in three-beat patterns
Sing and conduct/beat time of songs in three-beat patterns
Improvise short rhythms in three-beat patterns using percussion instruments
Prepare a printing block from available resources (rubber/old slippers, wood, any other) using geometric shape motif
Improvise natural dye paste or artificial printing paste (Note: observe safety in improvising the paste)
Block print a full repeat pattern on a small fabric using contrasting colours
Neaten by trimming/stitching and ironing to make a small decorated table mat
Share the work with peers for critique and feedback for improvement
coreCompetencies: Creativity and Imagination — combines various techniques to creatively come up with rhythmic patterns and repeat patterns using block printing
Self-efficacy — applies composition techniques to create and improvise original rhythmic patterns
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — applies number concept when improvising three-beat patterns
Agriculture — applies the skills of finishing by trimming/stitching and ironing in making a table mat
scopeNotes: include: exact note-value set is crotchet, (pair of) quaver(s), minim, dotted minim, semibreve, and their rests
include: exact French rhythm names are taa, ta-te, taa-aa, taa-aa-aa, taa-aa-aa-aa
include: pattern making is specifically block printing with a geometric shape motif, full repeat pattern, on fabric (table mat)
subStrands.notes: Split into 2 skills: rhythm notation/composition (note values, French rhythm names, 3-beat improvisation) and block-print pattern making (geometric motif, full repeat pattern) — two named distinct techniques.

subStrands.name: 1.5 Weaving
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify a plain weave for familiarity
Prepare materials and tools for weaving
Weave a mat using plain weave on a serrated card loom
Appreciate own and peers' woven items
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is recycling beneficial to the environment?
learningExperiences: Research in virtual and actual sources to identify a plain weave
Collect and prepare recyclable materials for weaving such as yarns, fibres among others
Make a serrated card loom on a stiff material and a shuttle
Weave a mat/scarf using a serrated card loom with emphasis on colour variation
Finish the mat/scarf by cutting and tying the tassels
Display and positively critique each other's woven items for reflective feedback
coreCompetencies: Critical thinking and problem solving — weaves a mat/scarf using a plain weave on a serrated card loom
Learning to learn — acquires new skill to make a mat or scarf using plain weaving technique
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — measures and cuts to make a serrated card loom
scopeNotes: include: plain weave is specifically 1/1 or 2/2 interlacing on a serrated card loom (small spaces)
subStrands.notes: Kept as one skill — a single technique.

subStrands.name: 1.6 Gymnastics
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the cartwheel skill in gymnastics
Perform the cartwheel skill in gymnastics
Perform 3-action sequence in cartwheel, forward roll and swan balance in gymnastics
Appreciate the action sequence of gymnastics for enjoyment
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are sequences performed in Gymnastics?
learningExperiences: Watch a video or live performance of a cartwheel in gymnastics and talk about how it is done
Demonstrate the cartwheel skill in gymnastics
Practise the cartwheel skill
Demonstrate sequencing of cartwheel, forward roll, and swan balance
Practise a 3-action sequence of cartwheel, forward roll, a swan balance while observing safety
Observe peers' gymnastic performance and give feedback
coreCompetencies: Learning to learn — acquires the skills of combining cartwheel, forward roll and swan balance to perform a 3-action sequence
Critical thinking and problem solving — practises and creates 3-action sequence of a gymnastics performance
Self-Efficacy — self-esteem is enhanced by being able to perform a 3-action sequence
linkedLearningAreas: Science and Technology — applies the concept of how the body works during performance of gymnastic activity
scopeNotes: include: the 3-action sequence order is specifically cartwheel → forward roll → swan balance
subStrands.notes: Kept as one skill — a single technique (cartwheel) building into one named 3-action sequence.

subStrands.name: 1.7 Melody
specificLearningOutcomes: Sing the sol-fa syllables doh to doh1 ascending and descending
Perform the sol-fa ladder using Kodaly hand signs
Aurally recognise sol-fa sounds doh to doh1 in familiar melodies
Compose short melodies within the range of doh to doh1
Write the sol-fa syllables using calligraphy lettering
Appreciate melodies created by self and others
keyInquiryQuestions: How can melodies be made interesting during composition?
learningExperiences: Sing sol-fa syllable doh to doh1 ascending and descending with accuracy in pitch
Imitate sol-fa pitches sung or played on a melodic instrument for pitch discrimination
Listen to and sing familiar songs within the d-d1 range using sol-fa syllables
Practise singing and performing the sol-fa ladder using Kodaly hand signs
Apply composition techniques to compose original melodies based on sol-fa syllables d r m f s l t d1
Use calligraphy lettering to add sol-fa syllables to created rhythms to form a melody
Record or present the created melodies to peers for review and improvement
coreCompetencies: Creativity and Imagination — makes thoughtful choices in selecting sol-fa syllables and note values to combine to create melodies
Critical thinking and Problem solving — listens and identifies sol-fa sounds in melodies and interprets hand signs
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — applies number and sequencing concepts learnt in combining sol-fa syllables in stepwise and leaps motion
English — uses vowels to sing the sol-fa syllables in ascending and descending order
scopeNotes: include: composition techniques are specifically narrow leaps (thirds), stepwise motion, repetition, variation and appropriate ending
include: full sol-fa range is doh, re, me, fah, soh, lah, te, doh1 (d r m f s l t d1)
subStrands.notes: Kept as one skill — content is unified around one scale/range even though several sub-skills (singing, hand signs, aural recognition, composition, notation) are named.

subStrands.name: 2.1 Athletics
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics
Perform the sail technique in Long jump for skills acquisition
Perform the scissors technique in High jump for skills acquisition
Appreciate Long jump and High jump techniques in athletics for enjoyment
keyInquiryQuestions: How is the jumping skill useful in athletics?
Why is it important to maintain a pace in athletics?
learningExperiences: Watch a virtual or live performance of a Long jump and High jump, and keenly observe sail technique in long jump and scissors technique in high jump
Demonstrate the sail technique in Long jump while observing safety
Practise the sail technique in Long jump while observing safety
Demonstrate the scissors technique in High jump, while observing safety
Practise the scissors technique in High jump while observing safety
Observe each other's performance in Long jump and High jump and give feedback
Display own and others' performance in Long jump and High jump and share feedback
coreCompetencies: Digital literacy — operates digital devices while watching performances
Creativity and Imagination — applies tactics while practising the sail technique and scissors technique
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — measures and appraises their performance accordingly
scopeNotes: include: exactly two named techniques — sail technique (Long jump), scissors technique/scissor style (High jump)
subStrands.notes: Kept as one skill — two field events, same 'jumping technique' theme.

subStrands.name: 2.2 Descant Recorder
specificLearningOutcomes: Play notes C to D1 on the descant recorder with appropriate playing techniques
Play a melody within the range of C to D1 on the descant recorder
Play the main melody of the Kenya National Anthem on the descant recorder
Show interest in playing the descant recorder
keyInquiryQuestions: How can a good tone be produced on a descant recorder?
learningExperiences: Observe and interpret the Baroque fingering chart of the notes C D E F G A B C1 and D1
Individually and in groups practise playing the notes C D E F G A B C1 D1 ascending and descending on the descant recorder with appropriate playing techniques
Practise playing melodies based on notes C D E F G A B C1 and D1 on the descant recorder applying playing techniques and hygiene measures
Present melodies before peers for critique and improvement
Search, watch videos and practise playing melodies on the descant recorder
Listen to and play the main melody of the Kenya National Anthem
coreCompetencies: Learning to learn — takes the initiative to learn how to play notes and melodies on the descant recorder
Citizenship — plays the main melody of the Kenya National Anthem on the descant recorder
linkedLearningAreas: Agriculture — applies hygiene measures learnt during use and after playing the descant recorder
scopeNotes: include: full note range is C D E F G A B C1 D1 (Baroque fingering)
include: playing techniques are specifically fingering, tonguing and posture
include: explicit repertoire piece named — the Kenya National Anthem's main melody

subStrands.name: 2.3 Indigenous Kenyan Instrumental Ensembles
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify the categories of indigenous Kenyan instrumental ensembles
Describe factors to consider when playing in an instrumental ensemble
Play a selected instrument in an ensemble using appropriate techniques
Appreciate the role of Kenyan indigenous musical instruments in performance
keyInquiryQuestions: How can one play an instrument as part of an instrumental ensemble?
learningExperiences: Observe actual/virtual samples of performance of Kenyan indigenous instrumental ensembles and classify them
Collaboratively identify the instruments that form part of the categories of the instrumental ensembles
Brainstorm on factors to consider for successful playing in an indigenous Kenyan instrumental ensemble
Select an instrument to perform in a Kenyan Indigenous Instrumental ensemble
Tune the selected instrument using appropriate technique
Handle with care while practising and playing a selected instrument in a Kenyan indigenous Instrumental ensemble
coreCompetencies: Citizenship — interacts with and plays indigenous Kenyan musical instruments in an ensemble
Communication and collaboration — teams up with peers to perform as an ensemble
linkedLearningAreas: Indigenous Languages — interacts with different musical instruments from indigenous Kenyan communities
Social Studies — interacts with musical instruments from different Kenyan Indigenous communities
scopeNotes: include: three named ensemble categories — percussion, wind, string ensemble

include: seven named factors to consider — choosing an appropriate instrument, tuning, playing technique, tempo, synchrony with other instrumentalists, accuracy in rhythm/melody, improvisation of rhythms and melodies
subStrands.notes: Kept as one skill — pool floor easily met via the 3 categories x 7 factors matrix.

subStrands.name: 2.4 Indigenous Kenyan Craft — Pottery
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify pottery items made using slab technique
Model a vase using slab technique for expression
Decorate a modelled item for aesthetic enhancement
Appreciate pottery as an indigenous Kenyan craft
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are clay items dried under the shade?
learningExperiences: Observe actual/virtual samples of indigenous Kenyan pottery items and identify items made using slab technique
Responsibly source clay from the environment (anthills, riverbanks among others)
Collaboratively prepare the clay by kneading and wedging
Roll clay into slabs of equal uniform thickness
Cut slabs of clay (rectangular and circular) and join to form a vase
Finish the vase by burnishing and stamping
Leave to dry under shade
Display and talk about own and others' modelled item
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration — works in a group to prepare the clay by kneading and wedging
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — exploits natural resources to source clay from the environment such as anthills, riverbanks
scopeNotes: include: clay preparation steps — source, knead, wedge, roll into equal-thickness slabs, cut (rectangular + circular), join, finish by burnishing/stamping, dry under shade (not direct sun)

subStrands.name: 2.5 Swimming (Optional — Either)
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the body position in breaststroke
Perform breaststroke in swimming for skill acquisition
Acknowledge performing breaststroke skill in swimming
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are swimming skills considered as survival skills?
learningExperiences: Watch a virtual or actual performance to observe breaststroke in swimming
Demonstrate breaststroke skill
Practise breaststroke skills while observing safety
Apply the skill of breaststroke in swimming game
Observe each other swim using breaststroke and give feedback
coreCompetencies: Self-efficacy — expresses water confidence as they practise the skill of breaststroke
Learning to learn — acquires new skill of breaststroke while practising in the swimming pool
linkedLearningAreas: Integrated Science — uses the knowledge of floatation to perform breaststroke in swimming
scopeNotes: The design presents 2.5 as an EITHER/OR choice between Swimming and Indigenous Kenyan Games — a real school picks one. This app builds skills for BOTH named options (matching the precedent already set by Grade 8 Creative Arts and Sports, which shipped both swimming.ts and indigenousGames.ts), since offline practice content isn't scarce the way a school's pool access is.

subStrands.name: 2.5 Indigenous Kenyan Games — Floor games (Optional — Or)
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify types of indigenous floor games played in Kenya
Perform different indigenous floor games for skill acquisition
Execute indigenous floor games to a musical rhythm for enjoyment
Appreciate the role played by indigenous floor games for fitness and health
keyInquiryQuestions: How do floor games enhance physical fitness?
Why are floor games considered as indigenous?
learningExperiences: Watch a virtual or live demonstration of indigenous floor game and identify the skills observed
Demonstrate indigenous floor games while observing safety
Practise indigenous floor games while observing safety
Practise different types of indigenous floor games while combining it to a musical rhythm
Talk about the role of indigenous floor games in enhancing fitness with peers
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration — works with others in performing indigenous floor games
Learning to learn — acquires and masters skills in floor games
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — keeps counting during practise of indigenous floor games
scopeNotes: The design does not enumerate specific named floor games (e.g. bao/ajua) in the Suggested Learning Experiences text itself — treated as a genuine content gap in the source; the skill should use commonly-documented Kenyan indigenous floor games (e.g. bao/ajua, kimbo/hopscotch-style games) rather than inventing unnamed ones, and should flag this as a source-thin area rather than silently padding it.

subStrands.name: 3.1 Analysis of Creative Arts works
specificLearningOutcomes: Create a catalogue of the exhibited artworks
Discuss the use of elements of music in a song
Discuss messages in songs
Participate in sporting events for enjoyment
Value analysing Creative Arts works drawn from various cultural backgrounds
learningExperiences: Visit virtual or actual art establishments for inspiration
Create a catalogue of the exhibited artworks indicating artist's name, type of artwork, media/material
Interpret works of art displayed by taking into account: type of art, material, media, meaning, techniques, aesthetic
Reflect on the analysed work of art for inspiration and mentorship

Listen to a variety of songs addressing Pertinent and Contemporary Issues such as climate, road safety and identify the type of song, discuss how different elements of music are used using appropriate terminology
Listen to and identify the message/values in the songs
Discuss the texture and structure of the songs
Listen to/refer to specific music and relate it to experiences or events in life
Participate in Football, Athletics, Volleyball, Rounders, Gymnastics and Swimming events for fun and inter-class/inter-school championships
Appreciate the sports performances with focus on fair play and observance of code of conduct to enhance sportsmanship
coreCompetencies: Critical thinking and problem solving — listens to and describes how the different elements of music are used in songs using appropriate terminologies and critiques artworks
Digital Literacy — interacts with digital technology to watch videos of songs and sports skill execution
Citizenship — visits community galleries or cultural centres to see artworks done by other local artists
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — visits community and virtual galleries to see artworks related to art techniques
scopeNotes: include: seven named elements of music — pitch, melody, rhythm, dynamics, tempo, texture (monophonic and homophonic texture) and structure (AB, ABA)
include: artwork catalogue must indicate artist's name, type of artwork, media/material
include: named sporting events for appreciation — Football, Athletics, Volleyball, Rounders, Gymnastics, Swimming
include: sportsmanship focus is specifically fair play and code-of-conduct observance
subStrands.notes: Kept as one skill despite breadth (visual-art catalogue + music-elements analysis + sports appreciation) — matches the Grade 7/Grade 8 Creative Arts and Sports precedent of a single 'analysis.ts' file for the whole Appreciation strand.
